l-001.evidence: The seq-1 detail query returns 16 rows in the observed window, all clustered 11:04:06–11:04:44, of which 12 carry event.outcome=failure with messages "Invalid user dev.dana from 172.18.0.11 port …", "Failed password for invalid user dev.dana … ssh2", and "pam_unix(sshd:auth): authentication failure; … rhost=172.18.0.11"; the two live controls (C-14d, C-21d) return 6 rows each, every one event.outcome=success with message "Accepted password for sre.ben …" and zero failures. The distinction is carried by event.outcome (failure vs success), user.name (dev.dana / " dev.dana" vs sre.ben) and the message text itself, none of which are unstable-identifier columns — source.ip 172.18.0.11 is excluded from the comparison per environment_notes but is not needed. Seq 0 corroborates: four STATS groups totalling 12 failed and 4 accepted (the accepted rows being "pam_unix … check pass; user unknown" with null source.ip/user.name), versus a single control group of accepted=6 / failed=0 for sre.ben. Seq 2 disagrees with its siblings — it returns row_count 0 for Accepted lines while both live controls return 6 Accepted rows for sre.ben — so the lead's queries are heterogeneous, but the union is unambiguously present.

l-002.evidence: All three queries surface a 2026-07-26 burst absent from every live control. seq 0 adds a day row `daily_count: 64, day: 2026-07-26` on top of the recurring `24 / 2026-07-03` row that appears in C-7d, C-14d and C-21d alike; seq 2 splits that 64 across three hour buckets (08:00=12, 09:00=48, 11:00=4), whereas every baseline burst occupies exactly one hour bucket (06-08T06:00=64, 07-03T12:00=24). seq 1 attributes it to `source.ip 172.18.0.11` with `first_seen 08:25:12` / `last_seen 11:04:44` — a ~2h40m span, versus the baseline bursts' 27s (172.18.0.21, 06:36:07→06:36:34) and 34s (172.18.0.13, 12:05:23→12:05:57). Since source.ip is an unstable identifier here, the distinction is carried not by the address but by the surfaced temporal fields: hour_of_day multiplicity and the first_seen/last_seen duration, which no live control matches.

l-003.evidence: Observed seq 0 (host.name == "db-1") returns 2 rows — 15 alerts of rule_id `v2-sshd-success-after-failures` (severity high, 11:08:28.824–11:08:28.857Z) and 1 alert of `v2-sshd-failed-auth-burst` (medium, 11:08:28.895Z) — while both live controls (C-14d 2026-07-12 and C-21d 2026-07-05) return row_count 0 for the identical db-1-scoped query; the distinguishing surfaced fields are host.name=db-1 paired with rule_id/severity, and host.name is the stable attribution column per environment_notes. The same two db-1 rows are the *only* rows in the unfiltered seq 5 and wider-window seq 6 payloads, whereas their live baselines carry 6 and 6/13 rows dominated by soc-playground Falco (311/640) and jump-box-1 sshd alerts, so the observed window both adds db-1 alerts and lacks the routine benign rules. Sibling queries disagree: seq 1 (`v2-cross-tier-ssh-pivot`) is empty against a C-21d baseline of 3 pivot alerts (dev-ws-1, web-2, null host), seq 2 (non-db-1 hosts) and seq 4 (null host) are empty against non-empty live baselines, and seq 8 is empty against 47/61 soc-playground Falco alerts — hence heterogeneous: true. Seq 3 is unreadable and carries no weight; it was not needed, since seq 0/5/6/7 already decide the lead.

l-004.evidence: The lead contains a single query, `cmdb.host-trust-edges` with param `host: db-1`, which returns a CMDB entity record — `name: db-1`, `role: db`, `criticality: prod`, `owner: team.data`, `change_window: sat 04:00-06:00 UTC`, `trust_edges_out: []`, and three `users` entries (svc.monitoring, svc.backups, svc.config-mgmt) — not an event stream. Per `state_and_lookup_systems`, cmdb queries carry no `@timestamp` bounds to move, so the empty `baseline` ([]) is expected and is not a missing or dead-window measurement. There is no baseline-diff semantics to apply regardless of the record's contents, so the lead is tagged `state-only`. With only one decidable query, `heterogeneous` is null.

l-005.evidence: Query seq 8 (`FROM logs-system.auth-* | WHERE host.name == "db-1" ... event.outcome == "failure" | STATS BY source.ip, user.name`) is the one query whose observed window carries a distinction in a stable, surfaced field: it returns 3 rows with user.name values `dev.dana`, `null`, and `' dev.dana'` (leading-space variant), whereas both live controls (C-14d 2026-07-12 and C-21d 2026-07-05, each widened to a full hour) return row_count 0 — so failed db-1 authentications with these user.name values exist only in the observed window, and the C-7d control being dead does not matter because two live controls settle it. Its companion success query (seq 23) shows 35 source.ip/user.name pairs vs 1 and 0 rows in the live controls, but that query carries no @timestamp bound in the observed run (counts like 247958 in seq 24 confirm the observed elastic queries are unbounded), so it is not a clean window comparison. Every other difference — seq 3/17/22 (host.name sets keyed on host.ip == 172.18.0.11), seq 4/9/10/28/33/34 (zeek source.ip/destination.ip), seq 11/14/15/18/19 (host.ip, client.ip) — differs only in columns listed as unstable in environment_notes (host.ip, source.ip, destination.ip, related.ip, container.id, zeek.session_id) for a snapshot-restored stack, so those rows are not deltas; seq 0 is a CMDB roster (state-only) and seqs 1, 5, 6, 12, 13, 29–31 are unreadable.

l-006.evidence: Both queries in this lead are identity-system lookups (`identity.access-check` for dev.dana on db-1, and `identity.user-authorization` for dev.dana), and the environment notes state explicitly that identity queries return an entity record or current configuration rather than an event stream, carry no `@timestamp` bounds to move, and therefore have no control and no baseline-diff semantics. Consistent with that, `baseline` is an empty list — not a measured empty window, but the absence of any baseline construct for this system. The observed payloads are configuration facts: seq 0 returns `authorized: false`, `via: null`, `role: developer`, `sudo: false`, `shell: null`; seq 1 returns `enabled: true`, `realm_role: developer`, `authorized_hosts: [dev-ws-1, jump-box-1, office-ws-1]` (db-1 absent), `sudo_hosts: [office-ws-1]`. Both queries agree in kind, so the lead is uniformly `state-only` and not heterogeneous.

l-007.evidence: Query seq 0 returns 70 alerts for rule_id "v2-sshd-success-after-failures" on db-1 (first_seen 08:28:04.891Z, last_seen 11:08:28.857Z, severity high), while both live control windows (C-14d 2026-07-12 and C-21d 2026-07-05, window_live true) return row_count 0 for the identical query — the `alerts` count and rule_id carry the distinction (C-7d is dead and carries no weight). Query seq 2 is host-scoped, not address-scoped, and surfaces a message value absent from both live baselines: "pam_unix(sshd:auth): check pass; user unknown" with count 16 and event.outcome success (08:25:10Z–11:04:41Z), whereas C-14d/C-21d contain only "Accepted password for sre.ben/sre.alice/sre.chen/svc.config-mgmt ..." rows at count 6; the `message` field is the distinguishing column. Query seq 1 adds 48+48+16+16+16 failures for user.name root and dev.dana/" dev.dana" against empty live baselines, though it is scoped on the unstable source.ip 172.18.0.11 so it is corroborating rather than load-bearing. The lead is heterogeneous: query seq 3 (success events from 172.18.0.11) is row_count 0 in observed and 0 in both live controls — no delta — and seq 4 is truncated (returned 5 of total 70), so it evidences nothing about absence.

l-008.evidence: The two sshd queries (seq 1, seq 2) return substantial rows in the operation window — seq 1 shows three host.name groups with accepted=0 and failed=144 (db-1, 08:25:10→11:04:44), failed=96 (web-1, 08:38:28→08:41:25) and failed=12 (web-2, 09:43:38→09:44:12), and seq 2 splits the same 252 failures into publickey-absent "other" (80/48/8) and "password" (64/48/4) buckets per host — while both live controls (C-14d 2026-07-12 and C-21d 2026-07-05, window_live: true) return row_count 0 for the identical query strings; the dead C-7d control is uninformative but not needed. The distinction is carried by `failed` counts and `host.name`, not by the unstable `source.ip`, which is a fixed filter constant identical in observed and baseline, so the environment's address-reassignment caveat does not erase the delta. No payload is marked truncated or unreadable. Seq 0 (Zeek connection logs) disagrees: observed row_count 0 against live baselines also at row_count 0, i.e. no delta on that stream — hence heterogeneous, but the lead's envelope is present on the union.

l-009.evidence: All four queries in this lead are `cmdb` queries (cmdb.list-all-hosts once, cmdb.host-trust-edges for dev-ws-1, jump-box-1, office-ws-1), which per environment_notes return current configuration/entity records rather than an event stream and carry no @timestamp bounds to move — hence the empty `baseline: []` is expected, not a missing measurement. The observed payloads are inventory records: seq 0 lists total 11 hosts with name/role/criticality/owner/trust_edges_out/users, and seq 1-3 return the same records for dev-ws-1 (dev, team.dev, trust_edges_out [jump-box-1]), jump-box-1 (prod, team.sre, trust_edges_out [web-1, web-2, db-1, dev-ws-1]) and office-ws-1 (preprod, dev.dana, trust_edges_out []). No payload surfaces any IP or address column at all, so 172.18.0.11 cannot be mapped to a host name from these rows; container addressing is also listed as unstable in this environment. All four queries are state-only, so they do not disagree.

l-010.evidence: Seq 0's observed 30-day payload has 9 rows versus 7/10/15 in the three live controls (C-7d/C-14d/C-21d), and two of the observed rows have no counterpart in any control: `failed: 16, source.ip 172.18.0.11, host.name db-1, first_seen 2026-07-26T08:25:10Z, last_seen 2026-07-26T11:04:41Z` and `failed: 4, source.ip 172.18.0.11, host.name web-2, 2026-07-26T09:43:38Z–09:44:10Z`. The distinguishing field is `host.name`: web-2 appears in no control payload (controls carry only jump-box-1, db-1, web-1), so the delta does not rest on `source.ip`, which environment_notes marks unstable; the failure timestamps on 2026-07-26 also fall outside every control window. Seq 2/3 do not add to this — their `accepted_count: 14` at jump-box-1 with first_seen == last_seen == 2026-06-12T15:55:04.801Z is exactly the row already present in the seq-0 C-14d and C-21d controls (accepted 14, failed 0, 172.18.0.11, jump-box-1), i.e. pre-window historical activity, and their own 1-hour controls returned 0 only because a bound was inserted into an otherwise unbounded query. Seq 1 (upper-bounded at 2026-07-26T00:00:00Z, no control supplied) contains no 172.18.0.11 rows at all, so the lead's queries disagree: one surfaces the delta, the rest look at quiet or pre-op ground.

l-011.evidence: Every query bounded to the operation day returns nothing: seq 2 (all SSH traffic, 2026-07-26T08:00–12:00) has row_count 0 while its live controls C-14d and C-21d return 5 rows each (e.g. 172.18.0.23→172.18.0.17:22, server SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.6p1); seq 7 (BY source.ip over 07-26) has row_count 0 while C-14d and C-21d each list 7 sources totalling ~2400–2600 events (172.18.0.22 at 672 and 581), and seq 5 likewise goes from 20 grouped rows in both live controls to 0. Consistent with that, the unbounded seq 8 gives max_ts = 2026-07-25T10:35:43.717Z over 143,371 total events, i.e. the zeek.ssh stream carries no rows anywhere past 07-25 — the stream is dark across the whole operation window, so the source-scoped queries (seq 1, 4) are empty on both sides and read absent, which is the disagreement recorded in heterogeneous. Nothing distinguishable ever surfaces for 172.18.0.11: the only rows for that address (seq 9, 07-25 window, 5+1+1 events; seq 10 all-time) carry zeek.ssh.client values SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.6p1 Ubuntu-3ubuntu13.16 / SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_8.9p1 Ubuntu-3ubuntu0.15 with chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com and umac-64-etm@openssh.com — identical to baseline values — and no hydra/medusa/paramiko-style string appears in any payload, while the addresses themselves are listed as unstable identifiers and cannot evidence a delta.
